goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — P1 (anchor: 95; code: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));`): this validation path never marks the matching code consumed or persists an updated credential, so an external-storage user can reuse every recovery code indefinitely, violating the one-time recovery-code invariant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), when validating recovery codes (lines 295-310), the code only checks if the input matches any stored code via `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` but never removes/marks the used code as consumed or updates the stored credential. This means the same recovery code can be reused multiple times, which violates the fundamental security property that recovery codes should be one-time use only. The local storage path in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator properly handles code consumption by updating the credential model, but this external storage validation path does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:217 — P2, confidence 100, anchor 100, code `if (isOTPType(credentialType)) { ... } else { log.infof("Unsupported to disable credential of type: %s", credentialType); }`: disabling the newly supported recovery-code credential is a no-op, so an administrator cannot revoke recovery codes held by this user-storage provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE in supportsCredentialType(), updateCredential(), isConfiguredFor(), isValid(), and getCredentials() methods. However, the getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() method at line 217 only handles OTP credentials and logs 'Unsupported to disable credential of type' for anything else. Since recovery codes are now a supported credential type but cannot be disabled, administrators cannot revoke recovery codes for users in this storage provider. This is a functional gap in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:255 — P2, confidence 100, anchor 100, code `if (myUser != null && myUser.otp != null) { types.add(CredentialModel.OTP); }`: the disableable-credential gate advertises only OTP even when recovery codes exist, so clients cannot discover recovery codes as a type they may disable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references line 255 and claims there's an issue with getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only advertising OTP. However, looking at the diff, the getDisableableCredentialTypesStream method is not modified in this diff - it's existing code that only shows context. The diff adds support for recovery codes in other methods (getCredentials, isConfiguredFor, isValid, updateCredential) but the getDisableableCredentialTypesStream method was not part of the changes. This is existing behavior, not something introduced by this diff. Additionally, recovery codes are typically not 'disableable' credentials in the same way OTP is - they are one-time use codes that get consumed rather than disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — P1 (anchor: 92; code: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`): the newly added federated provider accepts a matching recovery code without consuming or marking it used, so a supposedly one-time code can successfully authenticate repeated browser logins.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test provider's isValid method at line 340 only checks if the recovery code matches but doesn't consume/remove it from the list. However, this is in a TEST provider (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage in testsuite-providers), not production code. The test provider is explicitly designed for backwards compatibility testing, not for production use. While the observation is technically accurate about the test code behavior, it's not a production bug - it's a limitation in test infrastructure that may or may not matter depending on test requirements. The real production credential handling is in RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider which properly consumes codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — [P2] `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` authenticates a matching recovery code without consuming it (and `getCredentials` recreates all codes as unused), so a stolen or previously used recovery code can be replayed indefinitely to bypass the intended one-time MFA recovery factor.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the recovery code validation at line 340 only checks if the code exists in the list but never removes/consumes it. The code does `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()));` which validates the code but doesn't mark it as used. Additionally, getCredentials() recreates the credential model from the stored data without tracking which codes have been used. This means the same recovery code can be reused multiple times, defeating the one-time nature of recovery codes. This is a security bug in the test user storage provider.
